title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two sisters from Rio Arriba County have sued the city of Española, claiming police illegally stopped them after a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate. On July 23, officers pulled over 21-year-old Jaclynn Gonzales and her 12-year-old sister on Calle Duran because the camera flagged their car as stolen in Rio Rancho. The plate actually ended in 2, but the camera read it as 7. The lawsuit says officers handcuffed both sisters and put them in separate police cars before realizing the mistake, even after Jaclynn asked them to call the girls' mother, who lived nearby.

The sisters, represented by attorney Sheri Raphaelson, are seeking unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, and restricted movement. Raphaelson filed a similar case in April for Adam Pacheco, then 17, who was forced to kneel with his hands on his head after being wrongly linked to an armed robbery. The city, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment. The lawsuits were filed January 3 in state District Court, but no next hearing date was given.
